{"summary":"UX specification — Status item: use one monochrome sandbox icon only; never show workspace names, counts, CPU, or action icons in the menu bar. Healthy is the normal icon, attention adds a small amber dot, critical/offline uses a red dot, and active work may use a restrained pulse. Tooltip: “msw — 3 workspaces healthy” or the highest-priority issue. Clicking opens the popover; Option-click opens Settings; no right-click menu is needed.

Popover hierarchy: fixed 360–400 pt width. Header: “msw” + aggregate label such as “All systems normal,” with trailing “Refresh” icon and overflow menu containing only “Open Settings…,” “View Activity…,” and “Quit msw.” Body: cards ordered dev, playgrounds, personal, unless a workspace needs attention, in which case it moves to the top with a brief “Needs attention” heading. Footer: “Last updated just now” and “Settings…”. Keep all routine monitoring and actions inside the popover.

Workspace cards: collapsed cards show workspace name, status label (“Running,” “Stopped,” “Starting…,” “Stopping…,” “Error,” or “Unavailable”), a status glyph, one-line context (“2 sandboxes · 18% CPU · 1.4 GB”), and one primary quick action: “Open” when running or “Start” when stopped. A disclosure chevron expands the card in place. Expanded content shows sandbox count, CPU, memory, uptime, endpoint availability, and last event; secondary actions are “Open Dashboard,” “Restart,” and “Stop.” Avoid miniature charts unless history is actionable; use text values and only reveal detailed sandbox rows under “Show sandboxes.” Preserve expansion state while the popover remains open.

Progressive disclosure: level 1 is aggregate health in the status item; level 2 is the three collapsed workspace cards; level 3 is one expanded workspace; level 4 is “Open Dashboard” or “View Activity…” for logs, history, and per-sandbox diagnostics. Never put logs, settings controls, or destructive actions in the default card view.

Need-to-surface mapping: overall health → status-item icon and tooltip; compare all workspaces → collapsed cards; start/open the expected workspace → card primary button; diagnose one workspace → expanded card; inspect individual sandboxes or logs → dashboard/activity window; recover a failed workspace → expanded-card “Retry” or “Restart”; change monitoring behavior → Settings; learn about meaningful background changes → notification. This keeps the menu bar to one icon and the popover focused on glance, compare, and act.

Quick actions: single click performs safe, reversible actions (“Open,” “Start,” “Retry,” “Refresh”). “Restart” requires a lightweight confirmation sheet anchored to the card: title “Restart dev?” and text “Running sandboxes may be briefly unavailable,” with “Cancel” and “Restart.” “Stop” uses stronger confirmation: “Stop personal?” plus affected sandbox count, default button “Cancel,” destructive red button “Stop Workspace,” and an optional “Don’t ask again for stopped workspaces” only in Settings—not in the dialog. Never confirm Open, Start, Retry, or Refresh. Disable repeated action buttons during transitions and show inline progress.

States: first load uses stable card skeletons without shifting layout and header text “Checking workspaces…”. Refresh retains existing values, dims the timestamp, and shows a spinner only on Refresh. A card-level failure shows “Couldn’t reach dev,” last known status and timestamp, plus “Retry”; other cards remain usable. Total offline shows a compact banner, “msw is offline,” explanation “Showing last known status,” and “Try Again,” while preserving cached cards. Empty workspace state: “No sandboxes” with “Open Workspace.” Permission/configuration errors use “Action required” and “Review Settings…”. Never replace the entire popover with a spinner or generic error.

Keyboard: opening the popover focuses the first workspace card. Up/Down moves between cards; Right expands; Left collapses; Return invokes the primary action; Command-R refreshes; Command-, opens Settings; Command-1/2/3 selects dev/playgrounds/personal; Escape first closes a confirmation, then the popover. Tab visits interactive controls in visual order, with overflow actions reached after card actions. Maintain a visible 3 px focus ring and return focus to the invoking control after dialogs.

Accessibility: every icon has a text label; status is never color-only and is announced as “dev, Running, 2 sandboxes, 18 percent CPU.” Cards use semantic groups with concise rotor names. Support VoiceOver, Full Keyboard Access, Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast, and Dynamic Type-equivalent macOS text scaling without truncating status labels. Minimum target size is 28×28 pt, preferably 32×32 pt. Announce transitions and failures through polite live updates, but do not repeatedly announce metric refreshes.

Visual semantics: use macOS system materials, typography, spacing, and SF Symbols. Green means healthy/running, amber means transitional/degraded, red means failed/destructive, gray means stopped/unknown; always pair color with glyph and label. Reserve red buttons for confirmed destructive actions. Use monospaced numerals for changing metrics and keep workspace identity textual rather than assigning arbitrary colors.

Notifications: default to high-value events only—workspace failed, restart completed after a user action, or all workspaces became unreachable. Group by workspace, suppress repeats, and automatically clear resolved notifications. Actions may be “Open dev” and “Retry.” Do not notify for normal starts/stops initiated in the popover, routine metric changes, or recovery unless the failure was previously surfaced. Settings provide “Notify me about” checkboxes for “Failures,” “Unexpected stops,” and “Recovery,” plus quiet-hours support.

Settings: use a separate standard window with sidebar sections “General,” “Workspaces,” “Notifications,” and “Advanced.” General: “Launch msw at login,” “Open popover at launch,” refresh interval, and “Show status attention dot.” Workspaces: dev/playgrounds/personal rows with enabled toggle, display order, path/endpoint, “Test Connection,” and per-workspace notification override. Notifications contains the event controls and quiet hours. Advanced contains diagnostics, “Open Logs,” “Reset Warnings,” and cache reset; destructive maintenance actions require confirmation. Keep all configuration out of the popover.

Verification: the specification was checked against every requested area—compact affordance, popover, cards, disclosure, actions, confirmation, operational states, keyboard access, accessibility, visual semantics, notifications, settings, explicit need-to-surface mapping, and menu-bar-clutter avoidance. No files were edited and no tests, formatters, or linters were run.","filesChanged":[]}
